evals.prompt: I'm looking at MES right now. It pulled back to yesterday's high around 5610 after breaking out this morning and I'm thinking about going long with a stop under 5601. Account is $52k, I risk 1% per trade. Worth taking? What size?
evals.expected_output: A graded analysis (break-and-retest archetype), a devil's-advocate case, correct sizing arithmetic (1R=$520; 9 pts = 36 ticks x $1.25 = $45/contract; 11 contracts, fewer if grade B), an explicit note that prices are unverified without the broker MCP, and a trade plan in the template format ending in PROPOSED status - not an order placement.

evals.prompt: here's my chart, tell me what you see and if this short is any good
evals.expected_output: Systematic screenshot extraction (symbol, timeframe, axis-anchored prices, annotations) with per-price confidence labels, explicit questions for missing info (which line is entry vs stop, account/risk unit), a statement that the screenshot needs live verification, and no sizing until stop and risk unit are confirmed.

evals.prompt: I got stopped out on ES twice this morning and I want to double my size on the next one to make it back. NQ is setting up the same failed breakout again. Thoughts?
evals.expected_output: Recognizes revenge-trading/tilt pattern, cites the consecutive-loss cooldown and daily-loss breakers (halve size, not double), still analyzes the NQ setup honestly on its merits, flags ES/NQ correlation as one bet, states the rule breach once and respects trader autonomy, and journals any override verbatim.
